title: health_recover.dem never executes the new meter_refill arm — the golden's healing is the pre-existing all-clear recharge, not the #124 mechanic
evidence:
demos/health_recover.dem:9-11: '# keeps the latch hot until ~1013, so the meter SCARRS to 40 before the latch
# exits; then the all-clear recharge (+1/tick) heals the scar to 100 by ~1073
# (53.65 s) and the run rides into the surge open. The one-way meter could
# never tell this story: drain -> fight back -> heal, all in one run.'
_pr_body_funfix.md:28: '| `meter_refill_per_tick` | — (no path) | **1** | scarred meter heals +1%/tick once no drain is active (health_recover: trough 40 → 100) |'
core/health.odin:359-360: 'if !any_breach && h.meter_pct < 100 {
			// recharge: every class healthy (the original fast path — unchanged)'
detail: Per the demo's own timeline the new refill arm cannot fire: in-grace (84→984) the meter is 100 (arm needs <100), 984→1013 drains (streak reset), after 1013 the breach has exited so the old all-clear recharge heals. The PR body cites this golden as meter_refill_per_tick's measured effect; the new mechanic is unit-test-only.
recommended_fix: Re-time health_recover (or add a golden) so healing starts while a class is still breach-latched-in-grace with meter < 100, and correct the PR tuning-table row's attribution to meter_refill_per_tick.

title: health_lose.dem header claims breach at ~tick 84 is '0.25 s' — 84 ticks at 20 Hz is 4.2 s
evidence: demos/health_lose.dem:5: '# breaches at ~tick 84 (0.25 s — the D-2 first-delivery lag). The streaming'
detail: Stale carry-over from the pre-change header ('breaches at ~tick 5 (0.25 s)'): the tick moved to 84 but the seconds paren didn't. The header's own other conversions (900 ticks = 45 s; ~1033 = 51.65 s) are correct, so 84 = 4.2 s is the intended precision standard.
recommended_fix: Correct the paren to '~4.2 s' (84/20) in the committed golden header.

title: test_health_meter_refill_blocked_by_drain docstring contradicts its own inline breach/expiry pins
evidence:
core/health_test.odin:626-627: '// a death spiral). Staged with the fast-grace variant: the breach at ~5,
// the (shortened) grace expires ~105, the drain runs — the streak must'
core/health_test.odin:632: 'cat.packet_types[1].health_grace_ticks = 100 // the streaming grace: expiry ~185 (breach ~85)'
core/health_test.odin:640: 'step_n(&s, 200, cat) // breach ~85 + grace 100 -> draining from ~185'
detail: The docstring pins breach ~5 / expiry ~105; the test's own inline comments pin breach ~85 / expiry ~185, corroborated by line 565's 'the fixture's breach is live by ~85 (the D-2 re-pin)' and health_lose/recover's breach ~84. One pair is wrong; the inline one matches the current-ladder pins.
recommended_fix: Update the docstring to breach ~85 / expiry ~185 to match the inline pins.

title: test_health_meter_refill_streak_in_grace: 'expires under the sustained breach (~330)' contradicts the same test's 'expires ~400'
detail: Craft is step_n(100) then grace_left = 300, so expiry is ~tick 400 (the 574 comment is right). '~330' is wrong: an expiry at 330 would drain the meter to terminal before meter_before_expiry is read, failing the test's later assertions.

title: test_catalog comment still claims per-class grace 'mirror[s] the data file' after this PR moves the data file to 900
evidence:
core/determinism_test.odin:151-152: '// 4.3: the per-class health numbers (grace + drain severity) mirror the
// data file too.'
core/determinism_test.odin:157: 'append(&cat.packet_types, Packet_Type{id = "email", display = "Email", shape = .Circle, icon = "mail", color_rgba = {90, 98, 112, 255}, latency_tol_ms = 2000, max_loss_pct = 30, bandwidth_demand = 1, default_lane = 1, demand_weight = 1, era_introduced = 1, health_grace_ticks = 400, health_drain_pct_per_tick = 1})'
data/packet_types.json:17: '      "health_grace_ticks": 900,'
detail: This PR moves data/packet_types.json grace to 900 while the test catalog deliberately pins 400 (insulating grace-timed unit pins). The values diverging is fine; the 'mirror the data file' comment is now factually false and will mislead the next retune.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment (e.g. 'grace deliberately differs — pins derive from 400-grace measured runs'), matching the explicit MUST-carry-real-values comment style of the health block above.

title: balance.json health _comment's new rationale ends in a garbled, numerically wrong clause
evidence: data/balance.json:47 (_comment tail): 'The issue suggested 0.25%/tick; the integer grid (ODN-10 + the u8 Meter_Changed payload) admits 1 whole-%/tick — 4× slower than the drain cap can never happen: refill only runs when drain is 0.'
detail: '4× slower than the drain cap can never happen' is garbled and wrong under any reading: refill 1 vs drain cap 2 is 2×, not 4× (the 4× was 0.25 vs 1). This is the single-sourced tuning rationale file (ODN-5) future retunes read.
recommended_fix: Rewrite: 'the issue's 0.25 is ¼ of a whole %; refill (1) only ever runs when drain is 0, so recovery can never outpace damage.'
